title: Asynchronous kernel pruning causing token reordering and softmax skew
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Symptom: After landing an asynchronous kernel pruning optimization that removes rarely-used kernel variants at runtime, we observe sporadic token reorderings in outputs and small but statistically significant softmax probability skews for bursty workloads. These divergences appear only under concurrent prefill + decode traffic patterns when pruning and kernel hot-swap coincide. The issue manifests as non-deterministic sample-to-sample differences (numerical drift) and occasional cache corruption traces in the KV window indexes.

Background: The optimization reduces memory and scheduling overhead by pruning kernel choices deemed low-utility based on recent telemetry. Pruning runs off the main serving thread and signals the scheduler to rebind model shards to remaining kernels. We suspect a race between pruning-induced kernel index remapping and the prefill/decode path updating KV indices and scoring buffers.

Why this matters: Affects production customers on Dedicated and Hosted tiers running high-concurrency chat workloads. Observed customer impact includes flipped token probabilities for ~0.2% of generated tokens and end-user visible token substitutions in ~0.01% of requests. This undermines determinism and can surface as quality regressions for safety-critical prompts.
repro_steps: Use the reproducer script: drive.google.com/drive/fake-repro-pruning-v1 (link in artifacts).
Deploy a small cluster with two kernel variants for the attention operator and enable async kernel pruning with threshold=0.1.
Run concurrent workload: 60% prefill requests (seq_len 1024) + 40% decode streaming requests (average decode length 40) at 400 rps.
Collect token-level diffs between runs with pruning on vs pruning off and inspect KV index logs and scheduler swap traces.
impact: customer-visible token divergences (~0.01% requests) and probabilistic softmax skew (~0.2% tokens); potential cache index corruption under stress; medium-to-high operational risk for Dedicated pools
hypothesis: Async pruning races with prefill/decode kernel binding updates, causing a stale kernel index to be used for an in-flight request which leads to misaligned KV offsets and small numerical differences in softmax results. Secondary factor: non-atomic update of the kernel-to-shard mapping and delayed KV-window fence. Tertiary factor: mixed-precision kernels having slightly different normalization constants amplify drift.
investigation: 02/11: Reproduced token reorder locally using reproducer with pruning toggled — confirmed divergence correlates with kernel-swap events.

02/12: Captured scheduler and KV logs; observed cases where kernel-swap completes while an in-flight prefill is still writing KV offsets; KV index increment occurs against old kernel mapping and later reads against new mapping.
02/13: Inserted lightweight atomic markers around bind/unbind; races reduced but not eliminated — indicates multiple interleavings (swap, prefill write, decode read).
02/14: Benchmarked mixed-precision vs full-precision kernels: drift magnitude increased when fallback from fp16->int8 occurred, suggesting quantization rounding exacerbates softmax skew.
02/15: Added additional asserts in staging that detected two KV writes to overlapping offsets during a single request lifecycle; raised immediate incident and enabled conservative mitigation.
mitigations: Hotfix (deployed 02/16): Disable async pruning by default for Dedicated clusters and make pruning opt-in per pool. Rollback reduces observed divergences to baseline.

Short-term: Add a per-request epoch check — requests tag kernel mapping epoch at start; apply a fail-fast if epoch mismatch detected during KV read/write (degrades latency slightly but prevents corruption).

Long-term: Introduce atomic swap for kernel mapping with memory fences and ensure in-flight requests complete against the mapping they started with; add unit/integration tests for mapping epoch transitions.
Test coverage: Add stress test harness that runs prefill+decode at scale with pruning enabled and asserts token-level determinism across repeated runs.
next_steps: Add epoch-tagging in request context and fail-fast path (Maya) - due 2025-02-20.
Extend CI stress tests with reproduce script and run nightly (SRE/QA) - Cycle 2025-W08.
Measure perf impact of atomic mapping and epoch checks; target <3% p99 latency regression at median load (perf team).
Follow-up postmortem and customer outreach plan once fix validated.
